# discard { #labdata.cache.discard }

```python
labdata.cache.discard(path, root=None)
```

Remove a cached object, and the readable links that stand for it.

The links have to go too. A hard link keeps the content alive after the
object is unlinked, and a readable path whose size still matches would then
be reused in place of the content fetched to replace it. Links are found by
inode, which covers the hard link and symbolic link cases; on a filesystem
that supports neither, [](`labdata.cache.link`) leaves copies, and those are
not found.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**path**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Path](`pathlib.Path`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Object to remove.

<code>[**root**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[Optional](`typing.Optional`)\[[Path](`pathlib.Path`)\]]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default}</code>

:   Cache root. Defaults to [](`labdata.config.cache_root`).

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[List](`typing.List`)\[[Path](`pathlib.Path`)\]]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The paths removed. The content is fetched again the next time it is asked for.
